tr-message: Choose a firmware distribution and build service, then select your device and version.
tr-customize: Customize installed packages and/or first boot script
tr-dtb-help: Describes the board and its hardware connections to the Linux kernel. It is not firmware on its own. Use the DTB for the exact board revision only if the boot instructions call for a separate device tree.
tr-cfe-help: Firmware for Broadcom BCM63xx devices that use the CFE bootloader. The 4M, 8M and 16M suffixes indicate flash capacity; EU and AU identify regional variants. Match the model and suffix to the device installation guide. This is not a generic LuCI upgrade image.
tr-uboot-help: U-Boot loads the kernel when the device powers on. It is not the operating system. Use this image only if the installation or recovery guide calls for a bootloader update; the wrong version can prevent the device from booting.
tr-cpximg-help: For devices that use the CPXIMG format. Follow the model guide to install it with sysupgrade in the stock firmware or with the built-in cpximg loader. It is not a generic LuCI upgrade file.
tr-eva-help: For installing or recovering firmware on devices with the EVA bootloader. Use this file only if the instructions for your model specify an EVA image, not for a routine LuCI upgrade.
tr-factory-help: For a first installation from the original firmware, check the model and hardware revision and follow the device guide for the Factory image. To update a compatible system already installed, use Sysupgrade instead.
tr-sysupgrade-help: To update a compatible installation, back up its settings, then use LuCI or the sysupgrade command. This is not a first-install image for stock firmware. Check the device guide before switching distributions.
tr-kernel-help: The Linux kernel without the system programs or configuration. Pair it with the matching root filesystem if your device loads them separately. The kernel alone is not a complete firmware image.
tr-initramfs-help: Boots a kernel and a minimal filesystem in RAM for installation or recovery. Booting this image alone does not install the system to flash; follow the device guide to make the installation persistent.
tr-rootfs-help: Contains only the root filesystem, with no boot partition. Use it to write a separate root partition when you already have a matching kernel. It cannot boot on its own; for a whole-disk install, choose a disk image that includes the kernel.
tr-ext4-help: The ext4 root filesystem is writable, so you can edit system files directly.
tr-squashfs-help: The SquashFS base system is read-only. Configuration changes are normally stored in a separate writable overlay.
tr-sdcard-help: For devices that boot from an SD card. Write the image to the whole card rather than copying the file onto it. Check the target card and back it up first: writing the image overwrites its partitions and data.
tr-tftp-help: For installation or recovery through a bootloader that accepts files over TFTP. Check the device guide for how to enter recovery mode, which IP addresses to use and the filename the bootloader expects.
tr-x86-combined-help: Whole-disk image for x86 systems using legacy BIOS. Includes the kernel and root filesystem. Attach virtual disk files to a VM; writing a raw .img to a physical disk overwrites its partitions.
tr-x86-combined-efi-help: Whole-disk image for x86 systems using UEFI. Includes EFI boot files, the kernel and root filesystem. Attach virtual disk files to a VM; writing a raw .img to a physical disk overwrites its partitions.
tr-other-help: Check the full filename against the installation guide for your model and hardware revision. Do not upload this file to LuCI unless the guide identifies it as an upgrade image.
tr-defaults: Script to run on first boot (uci-defaults)
tr-uci-drafts-help: Drafts are kept separately for each firmware distribution in this page. Build services for the same distribution share its draft. Reloading the page clears the drafts.
tr-rootfs-size-help: Leave empty for the device default. The allowed range follows the selected service. This depends on the device image layout and does not increase physical storage.
tr-rootfs-invalid: Enter a whole number within the selected service's size range, or leave it empty.
tr-asu-service-help: Changing distribution or service reloads devices, versions and default packages. Script drafts are restored per distribution. Advanced options are retained; check that custom feeds match the selected distribution. Selection is locked while a build is running.
tr-repositories-help: Enter a unique name and an HTTP(S) feed directory URL for the selected distribution. Version and platform placeholders are supported. The build service may restrict allowed feeds.
tr-repositories-mode-help: Append keeps the build server's existing feeds. Replace uses only the feeds listed below; include every feed needed by your packages.
tr-repository-name-invalid: Enter a feed name using letters, numbers, underscores, dots or hyphens.
tr-repository-name-duplicate: Each feed must have a different name.
tr-repository-url-invalid: Enter a complete HTTP or HTTPS feed URL. Check any placeholders.
tr-repository-keys-help: Paste one complete feed signing public key per entry, preserving line breaks (for example, a usign public key). The build server verifies the key format.
